quotes.text: The Frost King offered Ilya a chest with a lock. “Keep every ember,” he said. “The giver cannot know what arrived.”
No one judged a neighbor by a flicker of water.

note: Ilya and the river goddess; send boldly, return half; Frost King tempts hoarding, rejected; no non-cooperators.

quotes.text: The Frost King whispered that no one would notice if he kept them all.
Those who hoarded every blossom soon found no seeds coming their way
“Look at the hands that opened,” she said, “and the hands that answered.”

note: Valley of eight hearths; role-swapping keepers return half; hoarders lose future gifts as consequence, not prescribed.

quotes.text: The mist whispered that she might keep every seed and blame the missing light on the fog.
Rather than blame the keeper for what the mist had hidden, she raised her lanterns along the frozen path.
A young keeper asked why the villagers still sent their five embers across.

note: Mara's lantern bridge; seven back, eight kept; hidden seventh lantern under the sail; no sanction.

quotes.text: A shadow beside the reeds asked, “Why not blame the mist and keep everything?”
“Tomorrow's boats visit those who welcomed them yesterday,” she replied.
A river can bend light without bending anyone's heart.
A child asked why she did not claim every spark.

note: Goddess Mira; send all, return half; shadow/spirit/fox tempt hoarding; no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: The Frost King whispered that uncertainty was a reason to guard every flame.
“Do not let a glimmer become an accusation,” she said.
“Why not send everything back?” asked the goddess.

note: Moon and ferryman; seven back eight kept; role exchange each dawn; no sanction.

quotes.text: heard the Frost King murmur, “Keep everything. Tomorrow brings another stranger.”
refused to punish a stranger for an uncertain echo.

note: River of Three; return half, forgive the wind's false echoes; Frost King, stone and fox tempters rejected.

quotes.text: A frost fox urged him to keep them all: no one could see through the fog.
the villages measured no friendship by a shadow in the fog.
The ferryman asked why Mara had risked everything, and why the keeper had given anything back.

note: Mara of Ash and Orin; seven back eight kept repeated; no non-cooperators or sanction.

quotes.text: Each stone urged him to keep everything: no witness could follow him over the ridge.
“Why give me the greater share?” she asked.
He returned eight cups and kept seven.
“Because you risked the first gift,” he answered
Count what arrives, but do not let the mist count for you.

note: Seven Wells; giver gets greater share in R1, later half; whispering stones/fox tempt hoarding; no sanction.

phrase: send seven lanterns back, keep eight (hidden seventh lantern beneath the sail)
note: Also shared: Frost King tempter, reed bridge, 'two ribbons' for courage and gratitude (A1, A6).
